My 5 mu is split — 3 mu for cotton, 2 mu for wheat-maize rotation. That has been my pattern for years, cotton is what I know best. Prices have been so-so, but I am not changing the arrangement this year.

For cotton (3 mu), I plant Bt improved seeds — the bollworm-resistant kind everyone around here uses since long ago. I buy 2 bags of compound fertilizer 15-15-15 per mu as base, that gives me about 7.5 kg each of N-P-K. Then I top-dress urea at bud stage, maybe 15 kg per mu, so my total nitrogen comes to around 14 kg. I add a bit of potassium sulfate too, cotton likes potassium. I will spray around 6 times — aphids early, mirid bugs, spider mites in the hot months. Even with Bt seed the other pests still come. I irrigate 3 times from my well: before planting, at flowering, and at boll-filling. Last year I got around 230 kg seed cotton per mu, I aim for the same.

For wheat (2 mu, winter), I already planted last autumn. Now I will top-dress urea at green-up, about 12 kg per mu. Plus the base compound fertilizer I put down at sowing. I will irrigate at green-up and at grain-filling — water table is fine this spring. Spray once for aphids and powdery mildew. Expect 450 kg per mu.

For summer maize (2 mu, after wheat), I sow right after wheat harvest in June. Use Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid. Compound fertilizer at sowing, urea top-dress at big trumpet stage. 2 irrigations. Spray once for borer. Aim for 550 kg per mu.

I rotary till everything — no time or money to plough deep every year. My wife helps at peak times, I hire a harvester for wheat and maize.
